subject: Nimbus Retail — elevated 5xx/429, retry storm & credit proposal
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nimbusretail.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate (5xx/429) across inference endpoints — urgent

Marcus —

We started seeing a spike in checkout failures on Saturday morning (approx 09:00 PDT). Our telemetry shows large numbers of 5xx responses and 429s from the Redwood API across the recommendation and checkout validation routes. Total failed checkouts estimated ~4.2k over a two hour window; revenue impact is material.

Attached: nimbus_error_snippet_0803.txt (first 500 lines of logs). We need:
- Immediate mitigation (routing/rollback) to stop the outage
- Explanation of root cause
- Proposed service credit for the outage period

This is on our critical path for Black Friday prep; procurement and our CTO are watching. Please escalate.

— Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Site Reliability, Nimbus Retail
maya.patel@nimbusretail.com
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nimbusretail.com>, Nimbus Procurement <procure@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: Nimbus Retail — elevated 5xx/429 (incident INV-20260803)

Team —

Looping you in after a direct escalation from Nimbus Ops (Maya). They report a concentrated 09:00–11:00 PDT window with elevated 5xx and 429 responses leading to ~4k failed checkouts. Customer impact is significant.

Immediate asks:
- Neha: can you validate whether this is a serving-side regression (kernel/quantization change, autoscaler behavior) or something client-driven (bad retry/backoff)?
- Rishi: confirm if any model rollout or config change happened in the relevant accounts/pools and whether we had autoscaler churn on the Dedicated pool they use.
- Lauren: procurement/partner escalation — keep Maya and their procurement looped for any formal credit request.

Customer attached logs; I expect a short RCA and a mitigation plan (can we route them to a stable model variant or pause autoscaling) within the hour. Also start a conservative credit calc we can present (initial estimate only).

I am available for an exec call if needed.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nimbusretail.com>, Nimbus Procurement <procure@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation: Nimbus Retail — elevated 5xx/429 (incident INV-20260803)

Marcus, team, Maya —

Quick update from ops/serving: prelim findings point to a combination of factors:
- A client-side retry configuration change in Nimbus's SDK caused aggressive immediate retries on 5xx results (observed burst of concurrent connections) — logs show retry intervals of <200ms.
- Coincidentally, the Dedicated pool servicing Nimbus experienced rapid autoscaler churn during that window (two scale events back-to-back) which temporarily increased tail latency for a subset of inference hosts.
- The combination produced a retry storm and temporary resource exhaustion manifesting as 429s and 5xx.

Mitigations we are enacting now:
1) Applying a short-lived circuit-breaker on their route (limit concurrency 60% below current peak) and enabling graceful queuing.
2) Rolling back the most recent autoscaler tuning change and locking the pool at the previous stable size for 24 hours.
3) Working with Nimbus Ops to recommend SDK backoff defaults (we can push a temporary gate if they authorize).

Attached a one-page incident timeline: initial_incident_timeline.pdf.

Suggested customer-facing remediation and credit posture (initial): we propose a service credit equal to one week at 30% of the billable charges covering the Aug 3 incident window while we complete a full RCA. This is conservative but keeps commercial risk manageable; please advise if Sales/Finance want a different anchor.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head, Production Reliability — Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nimbusretail.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Procurement <procure@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation: Nimbus Retail — elevated 5xx/429 (incident INV-20260803)

Thanks for the fast triage. The mitigation helped: error rate returned to baseline after the circuit-breaker and autoscaler lock at ~11:05 PDT.

Procurement has asked for a specific credit number and a short written statement we can attach to our internal incident post-mortem. They also requested an executive-level assurance that we won’t see regressions during our Black Friday prep window.

I've attached a short CSV with our impact summary: ops-impact.csv. Procurement wants the credit to be stipulated in writing before they sign off. Please let us know an exact credit proposal and an SLA addendum we can review.

— Maya
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nimbusretail.com>, Nimbus Procurement <procure@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus — proposed credit & follow-up plan (Aug 3 outage)

Maya / Procurement —

Thanks for the patience. Per Neha's RCA and our commercial review, Redwood proposes the following:

1) Service credit: 30% credit applied to Nimbus's Redwood invoice for the billing period that includes Aug 3–4, 2026. This is intended to cover the direct impact window (cumulative ~2 hours of degraded service) and related retries.
2) Waiver: we will waive any burst charges incurred during the mitigation window that resulted from autoscaler churn.
3) Technical follow-up: a joint ops call (Redwood SRE + Nimbus Ops) within 48 hours to review SDK backoff defaults and a plan to ship a recommended client patch to Nimbus.
4) SLA addendum: Redwood will draft a short addendum that documents the incident, the credit, and a commitment to enhanced monitoring thresholds for Nimbus's account for the next 90 days.

Attached: proposed_credit_calc.xlsx and a Draft SLA addendum link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nimbus-incident. Once you confirm we will issue a formal credit memo and route a DocuSign for signature.

If procurement wants a higher credit, please state the requested percentage and we will escalate to Finance/Leadership for approval.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nimbusretail.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Procurement <procure@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus — proposed credit & follow-up plan (Aug 3 outage)

Marcus —

We can accept the 30% credit for the Aug 3–4 billing period and the waiver of burst charges. Procurement will sign the DocuSign once we receive the addendum language. Please include a short exec note (one paragraph) for our CTO. We also want the joint ops call scheduled for tomorrow morning (East Coast preferred).

Appreciate the responsiveness — the mitigation and plan look reasonable.

— Maya
